sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Indirect cellular ELISA confirmed surface display of the N-terminal HA-tagged full-length HCAR3 receptor (L3); no ligand-binding or signalling assay reported for the tagged construct specifically.
sites.rationale: HCAR3 carries no signal peptide; the topology landmarks place residues 1–28 extracellular, making the N-terminus the sole extracellular terminus of the protein. No residue number is stated in any ledger line, but exactly one extracellular terminus exists, so the junction is unambiguously computed as a prepend before M1 (insert_after_residue = 0). The N-terminal HA tag was confirmed at the cell surface by indirect cellular ELISA (L2/L3), providing direct surface-display evidence for this position. Python verification confirms residue 1 = M and residue 28 = K (last extracellular residue before TM1 at V29), consistent with a 28-residue extracellular N-terminal domain that can accommodate a short prepended tag. Full-length human HCAR3 cloned into pcDNA3.1(−) with an N-terminal HA epitope (YPYDVPDYA) and C-terminal FLAG tag; cell surface expression of the N-terminal HA-tagged construct was assessed by indirect cellular ELISA in transfected cells (L2, L3). A parallel construct in pcDps with the same dual-tag arrangement was also reported (L1). Additional full-length constructs for structural studies (L5, L6, L7) independently place a FLAG epitope at the extracellular N-terminus after an exogenous signal-peptide cleavage, further corroborating N-terminal extracellular tag tolerance.

sources.claim: The full length human HCAR1, human HCAR2 and human HCAR3 with an N-terminal hemagglutinin (HA) epitope (YPYDVPDYA) and a C-terminal FLAG-tag (DYKDDDDK) were inserted into the mammalian expression vector pcDNA3.1(−) (Invitrogen).

literature_notes: Seven ledger lines were evaluated. L1 and L2 both describe full-length HCAR3 with an N-terminal HA tag and a C-terminal FLAG tag; L3 explicitly confirms surface display of the N-terminal HA by cellular ELISA. L4 describes a C-terminal mRuby fusion used for trafficking studies; the C-terminus (residues 298–387) is intracellular per the topology landmarks, so this is recorded in other_positions. L5, L6, and L7 describe structural-study constructs (pFastBac, bRIL fusion) with an exogenous HA signal peptide followed by a FLAG tag at the extracellular N-terminus of the full-length receptor; these are full-length membrane-anchored constructs and independently corroborate N-terminal extracellular tag tolerance, but they do not add a new position (all converge on the same N-terminal prepend). No ledger line reports a tolerated insertion in any of the three extracellular loops (ECL1 85–101, ECL2 165–188, ECL3 258–273), so no internal sites are proposed. The C-terminal His tag in L5 is also intracellular and is not separately listed as it is redundant with L4/L1/L2 for the intracellular C-terminus.

literature_other_positions.note: C-terminal mRuby fluorescent-protein fusion on full-length human HCA3 used for internalization/trafficking studies; the C-terminus (residues 298–387) is intracellular per topology landmarks, so this is not a surface tag site.
C-terminal FLAG tag on full-length HCAR3 in pcDps; C-terminus is intracellular (298–387), confirmed by topology.
